text:
To undo your last git commit while keeping the changes in your working tree, use:

```bash
git reset --soft HEAD~1
```

This will:
- **Remove the commit** from history
- **Keep changes staged** (ready to commit again)
- **Keep your working tree unchanged**

If you want to keep changes **unstaged** instead:

```bash
git reset HEAD~1
```

Or use `git reset --mixed HEAD~1` (same as above, `--mixed` is the default).

**Visual comparison:**

| Command | Commit | Staged Changes | Working Tree |
|---------|--------|----------------|--------------|
| `git reset --soft HEAD~1` | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `git reset HEAD~1` | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `git reset --hard HEAD~1` | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

After running `--soft`, you can re-commit with:
```bash
git commit -m "New commit message"
```
